etymology: Phono-semantic: roof (宀) + 至 'to arrive' (phonetic シツ) — the space under the roof you arrive into: a room.
mnemonic: Walk under the roof until you can go no further (至): you've arrived in the room — シツ. The 教室 is the room the school day arrives at.

etymology: Compound: two bows (弓) with soft frayed decorations hanging from them — ornamental bows never meant to fire: weak.
mnemonic: Two ceremonial bows dripping with tassels: pretty, useless in a fight — よわい. Twice the bows, half the strength.

etymology: Pictograph: a head with its hair (the top strokes) and its face reduced to an eye — the head, and by extension the neck it sits on.
mnemonic: Hair on top, eye in the middle: a head planted on a neck — くび. The 首相 is the 'neck minister': the head of government.

etymology: Compound ideograph: grain (禾) + fire (火) — the stubble fires burning after harvest: autumn.
mnemonic: The harvest is in and the fields are set alight; smoke and gold everywhere — あき. Autumn is grain plus flame.

etymology: Compound: sprouts pushing up (an old form of 屯, worn into 三 + 人) under the sun (日) — the season of germination: spring.
mnemonic: Three shoots and a pair of legs racing up toward the sun — はる. Spring is the ground sprinting.

etymology: Phono-semantic: soil (土) + 昜 'sun rising high' (phonetic ジョウ) — sunlit ground: an open place, a site.
mnemonic: A patch of earth the sun picks out like a spotlight: the place where things happen — ば. 場所, 工場, 野球場 — every stage is soil plus light.

etymology: Compound: two bent human figures pressed together — originally facial flush and passion; from the color of the face came 'color' itself.
mnemonic: A blush spreading over a face: the first color anyone notices — いろ. Feelings leak out as colors; that's why 色 means both.

etymology: Pictograph: the heart organ with its chambers — three drops of blood around the central hook. As a component (心/忄) it beats inside every kanji of feeling.
mnemonic: A heart mid-beat, blood flying — こころ. Find it at the bottom of 思, 悪, 意: whatever the top does, the heart underneath feels it.

etymology: Phono-semantic: 亲 (a standing tree, phonetic シン) + 見 'watch' — the classic image: the parent up the tree, watching for the child's return.
mnemonic: Climbed up the tree (亲), eyes on the road (見), waiting for you to come home — おや. That worried silhouette is what 'parent' looks like.

etymology: Simplified from 圖: a bordered territory (囗) with its granaries and roads sketched inside — a plan, a map.
mnemonic: A framed sheet with X-marks-the-spot scratched inside: the map — ズ. The 図書館 shelves whole worlds folded flat.

etymology: Simplified from 聲: a hanging stone chime being struck, with an ear listening below — ringing sound: the voice.
mnemonic: A stone chime hangs from its frame; strike it and it answers — こえ. Your voice is the chime only you can ring.

etymology: Phono-semantic: 七 (originally the picture of cutting crosswise, phonetic セツ) + 刀 'sword' — the blade doing what 七 once drew: to cut.
mnemonic: Seven (七) slices of the sword (刀) — きる. 切符 is a ticket cut from the roll; 大切 is what you'd never let be cut away.

etymology: Compound ideograph: a person leaning into a sprint (worn into 土) over a flying foot (止) — arms pumping: to run.
mnemonic: Torso pitched forward, one foot barely touching ground — はしる. The whole kanji is mid-stride; that's why nothing in it stands straight.

etymology: Derived from 大 'big' with a dot added for emphasis — bigger than big: thick, stout.
mnemonic: 'Big' (大) after dessert: one extra dot at the belly — ふとい. The 太陽, the sun, is the plumpest thing in the sky.

etymology: Modern form of 體: person (亻) + 本 'root' — the body as a person's root and trunk, the base everything else grows from.
mnemonic: Your body is the root (本) your person (亻) is planted in — からだ. Take care of the trunk before decorating the branches.

etymology: Adopted as the simple form of 臺 'raised tower' — an old character combining 厶 and 口, long used for platforms and stands; now also the counter for machines.
mnemonic: A little podium: base block (口) with a speaker's arm (厶) resting on top — ダイ. Machines get counted on pedestals: 一台, 二台.

etymology: Compound ideograph: arrow (矢) + mouth (口) — an answer that flies from the mouth straight as an arrow: to know.
mnemonic: Ask, and the reply hits the bullseye before you finish the question — しる. Knowledge is a mouth with good aim.

etymology: Phono-semantic: soil (土) + 也 (phonetic チ) — the ground underfoot; the earth as terrain rather than dirt.
mnemonic: Soil (土) stretching away in a long winding tail (也): the land itself — チ. 地図 maps it, 地下鉄 tunnels under it.

etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 也 (phonetic チ) — water gathered in a hollow of the ground: a pond. The twin of 地 with water swapped for soil.
mnemonic: Same winding hollow as 地, but filled with water (氵): the garden pond — いけ. Where 地 ends, 池 reflects.

etymology: Variant of the older 荼: the plant (艹) over a phonetic reduced to a canopy on a tree-like base — the tea bush, and the drink that conquered the world.
mnemonic: A leaf (艹) drying under a little canopy on a wooden rack: tea in the making — チャ. お茶 time is when the kanji finally gets poured.

etymology: Simplified from 晝: a hand with a brush (聿) ruling off the hours of the sun (日) — the measured stretch of daylight: daytime.
mnemonic: A ruler laid across the sun: the bright hours, measured from bell to bell — ひる. 昼ご飯 lands exactly in the middle of the ruler.

etymology: Compound ideograph: the sun (日) rising through grass (the vertical strokes) while the moon (月) still hangs in the west — dawn: morning.
mnemonic: Sun climbing through the reeds on the left, pale moon not yet gone on the right — あさ. Morning is the shift change, caught mid-handover.

etymology: Pictograph: a long-tailed bird — crest, eye, folded wing, and the four dots of its tail feathers (灬).
mnemonic: Crest up, wing tucked, tail feathers fanned into four dots — とり. Remove one stroke (the eye) and the poor thing goes 烏, blind crow.

etymology: Phono-semantic: movement (辶) + 甬 'hollow tube' (phonetic ツウ) — passing through like water through a pipe: to go through, commute, connect.
mnemonic: The road becomes a tube and you slide through it, door to door, every day — とおる, かよう. 交通 is everyone in the tubes at once.

etymology: Pictograph: a leather cord wound around a stake in descending turns — sequence, order of birth: the one born after, the younger brother.
mnemonic: The cord spirals down the pole, turn below turn: he comes after you — おとうと. Birth order, drawn as a winding.

etymology: Compound: the tied-off ends of a rope (夂 — the year's thread finished) with ice (冫) beneath — the season that closes the year: winter.
mnemonic: The year's rope tied off, two icicles hanging from the knot — ふゆ. Winter is the calendar's final knot, frozen stiff.

etymology: Phono-semantic: bamboo (竹) + 合 'fit' (phonetic トウ) — bamboo tally-slips split in two: the half that fits yours is the answer.
mnemonic: Snap the bamboo slip in two, keep one half: the reply that clicks (合) back into it is the answer — こたえ.

etymology: Phono-semantic: 豆 'ritual vessel on a stem' (phonetic トウ) + 頁 'head' — the head on its stem of a neck.
mnemonic: A goblet (豆) balancing a big head (頁): don't tip it — あたま. When it aches, the vessel is overfull: 頭が痛い.

etymology: Compound: one cover (the frame) over one (一) mouth (口) — many people speaking as one under one roof: same, together.
mnemonic: One hood, one line, one mouth: everyone inside says the same thing — おなじ. 同じ! echoes the room.

etymology: Pictograph: a slab of meat with its sinew-lines inside. As a component it disguises itself as 月 (the 'meat moon') in 体-adjacent kanji like 腹 and 脳.
mnemonic: A cut of ribs hanging in the frame, marbling drawn as two little persons — にく. 焼肉: this kanji, grilling.

etymology: Simplified from 賣: taking out (出, worn into 士) what was bought (買, reduced to the cover and legs) — goods carried out to market: to sell.
mnemonic: A salesman (士) sets up his little stand (the cover) and runs (legs) after every customer — うる. 売り切れ: run after too well — sold out.

etymology: Phono-semantic: a sail-canopy (凡, phonetic フウ) over an insect (虫) — the ancients believed wind bred the insects it carried: wind.
mnemonic: A sail bellies out and a single bug rides the gust inside it — かぜ. Wind carries seeds, smells, bugs and fashions: 和風, Japanese style, is Japan riding its own breeze.

etymology: Compound ideograph: two footprints, one after the other (止 + a reversed foot worn into 少) — left, right: to walk.
mnemonic: Stop (止) a little (少), step, stop, step: that rhythm is walking — あるく. The 散歩 is the art of stopping slightly, beautifully.

etymology: Origin debated — a plow, or two boats lashed side by side. It has meant 'direction, side' since the oracle bones, and politely, 'the person over on that side'.
mnemonic: A weathervane with a crooked tail, pointing somewhere — ほう, the direction; かた, the honored person standing that way. あの方 = that way, that person.

etymology: Phono-semantic: woman (女) + 未 'not yet' (phonetic マイ) — the woman not yet grown: the younger sister.
mnemonic: A girl (女) with a 'not yet' (未) pinned to her: not yet as tall as you, not yet allowed to stay up — いもうと.

etymology: Compound ideograph: sun (日) and moon (月) shining together — the two lights of heaven in one character: bright, clear.
mnemonic: Sun and moon on at the same time: maximum brightness — あかるい. 明日 is the bright side of midnight: tomorrow.

etymology: Pictograph: a double-leafed gate, both doors on their hinges. As a frame-component it hosts whatever happens at the threshold (間, 開, 聞).
mnemonic: Two saloon doors still swinging — モン. Whoever stands inside this frame in a kanji is doing something at the gate: listening (聞), opening (開), measuring the gap (間).

etymology: Phono-semantic: a person (亻) under a cover (亠) with the moon (夕) tucked at their side — the dark hours a person spends under shelter: night.
mnemonic: Coat on the hook, someone home under the roof, the moon leaning at the window — よる. 今夜: tonight, the moon already in position.

etymology: Phono-semantic: 里 'village and its fields' + 予 (phonetic ヤ) — the open land beyond the last houses: plains, the wild.
mnemonic: Past the village (里) the fences stop and the grass takes over — の. 野球 is baseball: the game of the open field.

etymology: Phono-semantic: sun (日) + 翟 'pheasant with spread feathers' (phonetic ヨウ) — the shining of the heavenly bodies, adopted to name the days of the week.
mnemonic: The sun preening its feathered wings — a different plumage every day of the week: ヨウ. 月曜日, 火曜日… seven outfits, one bird.

etymology: Pictograph of debated origin — a bucket or a section of fencing. It has meant 'use, employ, task' since the earliest inscriptions.
mnemonic: A sturdy bucket ribbed with slats: grabbed every single day because it just works — もちいる, ヨウ. 用事 is whatever the bucket is needed for today.

etymology: Phono-semantic: jade (王) + 里 (phonetic リ) — carving jade along its natural veins: the inner pattern of things, hence reason, logic.
mnemonic: Cut the gem with its grain, never against: follow the hidden lines — リ. 料理, 理由, 無理 — cooking, reasons, and what goes against the grain.

etymology: Phono-semantic: 亜 — the cramped floor-plan of an ancient tomb chamber (phonetic ア) — + heart (心): a heart twisted into a cramped shape: bad, evil.
mnemonic: A heart squeezed into a tomb-shaped box until it warps — わるい. Villains aren't born; their 心 just ran out of floor space.

etymology: Phono-semantic: sun (日) + 音 (phonetic アン) — the sun muffled like a sound behind a wall: dark, dim; also 'by heart' (in the dark, without looking).
mnemonic: The lights go out and the sun becomes a sound you can only hear — くらい. 暗記: learning in the dark, eyes closed.

etymology: Compound ideograph: the sound (音) of the heart (心) — what the heart is saying before the mouth does: intention, meaning, idea.
mnemonic: Put a stethoscope to the chest: the heart is humming a plan — イ. 意味 is the meaning; 注意 is turning the volume up on it.
